transcript.text: Let’s narrow it down. Please keep the doors shut as much as you can to maintain the temperature. A fridge should be at 5°C or below. Chilled food that has been warmer than 8°C for more than about four hours is safest thrown away, and food that has fully thawed shouldn't be refrozen unless it's cooked first. Is it just the fridge that's warm, just the freezer, or both?
just the fridge. freezer's still freezing stuff solid

It can take up to a day for your fridge freezer to recover if a door was left ajar or if you placed a large amount of warm food inside. Please allow time for the temperature to stabilise naturally. Has a door been left open or not shut properly recently, or has a lot of warm food gone in?
no, nothing like that. its been getting worse over about a week. kids do open the doors a lot though

Thanks for letting us know about the doors staying shut. Please check the temperature dial or display to ensure the fridge is around 3–5°C and the freezer at -18°C, while confirming no holiday or eco mode is active. You can refer to the picture shown in the app for guidance on where these controls are located. Was a setting wrong or a mode left on (and have you corrected it), or was it all set normally?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
settings normal. fridge on 3, freezer -19, nobody's changed them. no eco or holiday mode that I can see

Thanks for confirming the settings are normal. Cold air enters through vents, often on the back wall inside. Please ensure food isn't pressed against them and that shelves aren't packed so tightly that air cannot move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
moved the food away from the back, no difference. hardly any cold air coming out of the slots at the back of the fridge

Thanks for letting me know it’s still warm. Please run your fingers gently round the rubber door seal on each door to check for splits, gaps, or sections that have detached, as well as anything preventing it from closing flat. Just look and feel along the rubber; do not pull or cut it. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
seals look fine, doors close properly

Thanks for checking the seal again. On most frost-free models, a fan pushes cold air from the freezer into the fridge. Open the freezer and press in the little door switch (or light button) — you should hear a fan whirr at the back. Just listen from the outside; do not take any covers off or touch anything at the back. Can you hear the fan running when you do that, or is it silent?
can hear a faint scraping/ticking noise from the freezer sometimes. not sure its a proper whirr. no burning smell or tripping if that matters

[Heading: Internal fan / airflow]
Thanks for letting me know the fan is still running. Since the freezer is cold but the fridge remains warm, it appears cold air isn't circulating from the freezer into the fridge compartment. This issue is typically caused by a faulty fan, an air damper problem, or an iced-up air channel. Because this requires safe internal inspection and repair, I recommend having an appliance engineer check the unit rather than attempting to replace parts yourself. In the meantime, please keep the doors shut to preserve the cold. For safety, any chilled food that has been warmer than 8°C for more than about four hours should be thrown away, and thawed food must not be refrozen unless it is cooked first.
